fixNow.title: Plaintext password comparison exposes credentials on any read access to the users collection
confidenceReasons: +0.25 Semgrep finding
+0.30 developer answer
+0.10 second independent source (2 kinds)
Confidence 65% (medium)
fixNow.attackScenario: app/data/user-dao.js:61 compares fromDB === fromUser directly, meaning the password field stored in the users collection is plaintext rather than a bcrypt hash (the commented-out bcrypt.compareSync fix at line 65 is disabled); anyone who obtains a MongoDB dump, backup, or gains read access to the users collection (e.g. via the memos-dao getAllMemos or an admin export) recovers every user's real password in cleartext, usable to log into other services where the same password is reused.

evidence.summary: Developer: Are user passwords hashed with a strong algorithm (e.g. bcrypt/argon2/scrypt) before being stored and compared, instead of being stored or compared as plaintext? -> No, passwords are stored/compared in plaintext
A stored password is compared with ===, which means it is stored in plaintext (a hash is compared with bcrypt.compare or similar, never ===). Store and compare a salted password hash.

mitigation.summary: Store salted password hashes and compare with a constant-time hash comparison.
steps: Hash passwords with bcrypt at signup/registration time in user-dao.js.
Replace the === comparison at app/data/user-dao.js:61 with bcrypt.compareSync(fromUser, fromDB) as shown in the commented-out fix.
Add a migration to re-hash any existing plaintext passwords on next login.

fixNow.title: Server-side request forgery via attacker-controlled url parameter on GET /research
confidenceReasons: +0.35 code evidence
+0.25 Semgrep finding
+0.10 second independent source (2 kinds)
Confidence 70% (high)
fixNow.attackScenario: app/routes/research.js:15-16 builds the outbound request as `req.query.url + req.query.symbol` and passes it straight to `needle.get(url, ...)`, and the client form in app/views/research.html:17 exposes `url` as an ordinary hidden form field an attacker can override, so a request to GET /research?url=http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/&symbol=iam causes the server to fetch cloud metadata or any internal-only host and reflect the response body back to the attacker in the rendered page.

evidence.summary: An outbound HTTP request is made to a URL whose beginning comes from the request, so an attacker chooses the host: server-side request forgery. Fix the host and pass only encoded parameters, or check the URL against an allow-list.

mitigation.summary: Enforce an allow-list for the outbound research host and stop accepting a caller-supplied base URL.
steps: In app/routes/research.js, remove the client-supplied `url` parameter entirely and hardcode the trusted base host (e.g. the Yahoo Finance quote endpoint) on the server.
If a configurable target is required, validate `req.query.url` against a strict allow-list of hostnames before calling needle.get, and reject anything else with 400.
Encode `req.query.symbol` before appending it to the URL rather than concatenating raw strings.

threats.title: SSRF via attacker-controlled `url` parameter on GET /research forwarded to needle.get
confidenceReasons: +0.25 Semgrep finding
Confidence 25% (low)
threats.attackScenario: An attacker submits GET /research?url=http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/&symbol=/ (or any internal address) instead of the expected https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/ prefix; app/routes/research.js:15 concatenates req.query.url with req.query.symbol with no host validation and app/routes/research.js:16 passes the resulting string directly to needle.get, causing the server to fetch and return internal endpoints or arbitrary external hosts, disclosing their content in the response body.

evidence.summary: An outbound HTTP request is made to a URL whose beginning comes from the request, so an attacker chooses the host: server-side request forgery. Fix the host and pass only encoded parameters, or check the URL against an allow-list.

mitigation.summary: Stop accepting an attacker-supplied URL/host; only accept the stock symbol and build the request URL server-side against an allow-listed finance API host.
steps: Remove the `url` parameter entirely; hardcode the finance API base URL in app/routes/research.js.
Validate req.query.symbol against a strict allow-listed pattern (e.g. ^[A-Z.]{1,10}$) before use.
If external redirect targets must remain configurable, validate the resolved hostname against an allow-list before calling needle.get.
